title: Book One · Chapter 124: A Sunday without Work
story:
On Sunday Mum closes her sewing bag after breakfast.

Ronan brings her a loose button from his shirt.

“Tomorrow,” she says.

“But it is here now.”

“So am I. Today I am going for a walk.”

Dad looks up from his tea.

“Where?”

“Somewhere without shirts.”

Dad looks down at his own. “That may be difficult.”

Mum throws a clean cloth at him. He catches it and laughs.

The air is warm after the rain. They walk away from River Street. Trees grow on both sides of this road. Ronan finds three leaves stuck together on the path. He lifts them with a stick and holds them like a little flag.

“No work,” Mum reminds him.

“This is a flag.”

“Then carry on.”

At a small open space, Dad buys two warm cakes. Mum breaks one in half for Ronan and herself. Dad tries to give her part of his too.

“Keep it,” she says. “I can count to two.”

“I hoped you could not.”

They sit on a low wall. Ronan eats slowly. Nearby, a father plays with his little girl. He is teaching her to throw a ball. She throws it behind herself twice. On the third try the father stands behind her.

“He is learning,” Dad says.

Mum laughs into her cake.

Ronan looks at Dad's hands. The little old cut is no longer there. There are new dark marks near his nails. Do those marks ever all go away? He wants to ask Dad. Instead he gives Dad the stick. The leaves are still on it, like a little flag.

Dad holds it up very straight.

“A fine tree.”

“A flag.”

“A fine flag tree.”

They take the long way home. Mum stops at a window full of cloth. She looks at a plain blue piece for a long time.

“For work?” Ronan asks.

“For me, perhaps.”

She does not buy it today. She tells Dad her ideas for the neck and sleeves. Dad listens. Ronan looks at the flat blue cloth. He looks at the cloth and thinks about a blue dress.

Near home they pass the old stall. Its shutter is down. A small sign tells customers to find Mr Qiu by the green gate. The sign has his name and a simple arrow. Ronan helped make that arrow yesterday.

He feels better when he sees it. Then he looks at the dark roof. A little water still sits in one low place.

“Will it all change?” he asks.

“What will?” Mum says.

“The street.”

Dad looks along it. Someone is painting a door. Someone else is washing a step. A boy carries bread home in both hands.

“Some of it,” Dad says.

Mum takes Ronan's empty hand. “Our dinner will be very late. Come on. We need to get home and cook.”

At the gate he puts the leaf flag beside the pot. By supper the leaves are already curling. He leaves them there anyway. Tomorrow he can draw them before they break.

Mum puts her sewing bag under the table. Ronan lays the loose button on top. It is safe there till morning. He does not ask again. Dad washes the three bowls while Mum sits in the doorway with her feet out in the yard. Her sewing stays in the bag. She does not get up to cook or clean. She just sits and looks across the yard. Ronan brings his book and sits beside her.

重点表达：carry on＝继续；sleeves＝衣袖；curling＝慢慢卷起。

情节提示：shutter＝店门前的卷帘；arrow＝箭头；flag＝旗子。

理解：1. Mum 星期天给自己留出了什么安排？2. Ronan 为什么喜欢看到旧摊位上的箭头？
